evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-14"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-14". The date is a plain calendar date with no time. POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/3 with {"dueDate":"2026-01-01"} changed the date (200). PATCH with only a title left the date unchanged. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} removed it (dueDate null, 200).
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate 2026-02-30, 15.10.2026, abc, an empty string and 2026-10-15T10:00:00 each returned 400 with an error message. PATCH with 2026-02-30 and with 'bad' also returned 400.
evidence.AC4: Today is 2026-10-15 UTC. I created a past-due open todo, one due today, one due in the future (later changed to a past date), one with no date, and a past-due todo marked done. GET /todos?overdue=true returned only the past-due open todos (ids 1 and 3). The due-today, no-date and done todos were excluded.
evidence.AC5: Loading / in the browser showed a <time> element with the date (yyyy-MM-dd) next to each todo that has one: 2026-10-14, 2026-10-15, 2026-01-01 and 2020-01-01. The todo with no date showed none.
evidence.AC6: On the list page, 'überfällig' appeared only next to the two past-due open todos (2026-10-14 and 2026-01-01). It did not appear on the todo due today, the one with no date, or the done todo with a past date.
evidence.AC7: The page has a checkbox labelled 'nur überfällige'. After I clicked it, the list showed only the two overdue todos (past and future2) and hid the other three.
